newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Rexrodt agrees with institutes' outlook.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt agrees with institutes' outlook.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Tuesday the forecast by six leading institutes of 2.5 percent growth next year was "fully in line with his own expectations".
"The cyclical weakness of last year is behind us," Rexrodt said in a statement. "The economic recovery, visible since since early this year, will continue next year."

The six institutes said in their half-yearly report that Germany's budget deficit would miss the Maastricht treaty target of three percent of gross domestic product next year, forecasting a deficit of 3.5 percent.
But Rexrodt said that the government "would do all possible to meet the intended consolidation goal of three percent to enter European monetary union."
Rexrodt added that the economic acceleration next year will not be sufficient to make a significant impact on German unemployment.

"The rebound in the economy is pleasing, but there is no cause to give the all-clear in economic policy," Rexrodt said, calling for a slimming of the state and a reduction in the tax and social security burden on businesses.
